changes.socket_rules: Apply every original socket domain predicate to socketpair too. Delete socketcall AND disable compat ABIs (see native_abi_only); AF_ALG=38, AF_VSOCK=40 and future domains remain denied without relying on AppArmor.
changes.additions: Exactly the rules with comment prefix Shellsmith:. Every addition is gated to amd64/arm64. Existing ordinary clone filters, clone3 ENOSYS, other capability/architecture gates and default EPERM are unchanged; archMap is intentionally tightened to native-only.
changes.removed_admin_rule_reason: Never enable the broad CAP_SYS_ADMIN syscall bundle; setns and new mount APIs must not become implicitly available.
changes.native_abi_only: Replace original archMap with native-only amd64/arm64 entries (no x86/x32/ARM compat ABIs). libseccomp rewrites compat socket rules to socketcall and discards the socket-family argument predicate; deleting socketcall alone is NOT sufficient. The pinned image and Codex packages are native 64-bit. Unsupported native platforms must be rejected by the launcher; additions do not match them.

codex.image: node:22.22.0-bookworm-slim; apt util-linux; npm @openai/codex@0.159.2; no apt bubblewrap.
codex.helper: The pinned image uses the npm-bundled bwrap, not an assumed Debian/system bwrap. Source identifies bubblewrap 0.11.2 with Codex changes. Codex prefers an external bwrap if present; adding one or overriding CODEX_VERSION requires a new audit.

npm_linux_x64.verified: Downloaded archive SHA-512 matches registry integrity; inspected bundled helper, not executed.

build_provenance.verification: Decoded registry-served SLSA statement; subject digest matches downloaded tarball and source commit matches audited tag. Sigstore signatures/transparency proof NOT independently verified.

npm_linux_x64.binary_inspection: ELF64 x86-64 static PIE; binary strings say bubblewrap built for Codex and setuid use is not supported in this build.

codex.arm64: Source-audited with the same native clone ABI; npm metadata exists but arm64 archive and execution not verified here.
required_operations: Raw clone arg0 exactly 0x38020011 (NEWUSER|NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWIPC|SIGCHLD), optionally 0x78020011 (+NEWNET). PID-inherit mode, UTS/cgroup/time namespaces and arbitrary clone flag additions are not enabled.
unshare arg0 exactly 0x10000000 (NEWUSER; secondary mapping for a non-root uid with devpts) or 0x10020000 (NEWUSER|NEWNS; Shellsmith util-linux preflight). No standalone mount/net/PID unshare.

mount arg3 exactly 0x44000, 0x8c000, 0x4c000, 6, 14, 10, 0xc0edd000, 0x9000, or 0xd000. Bind-remount requires 0x9022 with only optional bits 0x200c0d. This includes MS_MGC_VAL for newroot, devpts for --dev, read-only bind remounts and util-linux propagation.
pivot_root for both bubblewrap pivots; umount2 arg1 exactly 2 (MNT_DETACH).

uid_map/gid_map/setgroups writes, capget/capset, prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS), seccomp and ordinary process/file/network syscalls already have Docker rules; capabilities acquired in a child user namespace do NOT re-enable Docker includes.caps rules (resolved at container creation).

No setns, clone3 allowance, mount_setattr, open_tree, move_mount, fsopen, fsmount, fsconfig, fspick, umount, overlay-specific mount flags or mqueue flags are added. clone3 stays ENOSYS to preserve libc fallback to filterable clone.
codex.network: The current Game Master profile explicitly enables IP networking. This policy is NOT an egress firewall or a claim of no Internet/host-service access. The optional NEWNET path only creates a fresh namespace; setns stays denied. Preserve bridge networking (never --network=host), no Docker/host service sockets, devices or writable host mounts. Keep Codex own restricted filesystem and network filters; outer filters cannot relax an inner filter. AF_VSOCK/AF_ALG, socketcall and io_uring bypasses stay blocked.

deployment: Pass ["--security-opt", "seccomp=" + str(trusted_absolute_policy_path)] to docker create/run, never a relative cwd/user-controlled profile, shell interpolation or the provenance JSON. Docker CLI reads it on the client; it is not an in-container mount.

Resolve from trusted PROJECT_ROOT/docker/seccomp-codex.json, require a regular non-symlink file in the trusted checkout, verify its reviewed digest before use, reject missing/malformed/changed policy, and bind policy bytes to the source/image identity. For race resistance, open with O_NOFOLLOW and copy verified bytes to a private host temporary regular file used by docker; do not accept model-controlled paths or environment overrides. Do not pass unconfined on any failure.

Only native Linux amd64/arm64 are supported; reject other architectures and compatibility-ABI execution. Do not add capabilities (especially CAP_SYS_ADMIN), privileged, host namespaces, writable host mounts or additional devices. Retain normal capability bounding restrictions, proc/sys masks, LSMs and restricted Codex permission profile. no-new-privileges is compatible with the bundled non-setuid helper; validate it in the runtime gate.

Host must support unprivileged nested user/mount/PID/IPC namespaces, UID/GID mapping and required mounts. Keep existing util-linux preflight, but ALSO run a no-model pinned codex sandbox smoke with the actual game_master permissions before provisioning real credentials/model calls. Check successful allowed writes AND denied credential reads, symlink/proc-root escapes, outside writes, forbidden socket families and namespace reentry; launch failure is not proof of successful confinement.

Default Docker AppArmor explicitly says deny mount; seccomp cannot override it. Ubuntu/userns restrictions and SELinux may independently refuse the helper. Reject such engines, retaining confinement. Use an already-supported protected host backend or stop. An administrator-maintained confined LSM policy would be separate reviewed work; never choose apparmor=unconfined, disable AppArmor/userns restrictions globally, grant CAP_SYS_ADMIN or fall back to danger-full-access/legacy Landlock.

Classic seccomp cannot read pathname/filesystem-type/clone3 pointer contents or prove the caller is inside a particular user namespace. Flag-filtered mount permissions are available to all container processes, not just bwrap; kernel capabilities, namespace ownership and LSMs enforce their scope. In a child user namespace the kernel may permit other filesystem types with the same flags: this is NOT a path/type mount allowlist. Opening these previously blocked entry points increases kernel attack surface; keep kernels patched and require runtime validation. If that residual exposure is unacceptable, fail closed rather than broaden further.

validation.environment: Darwin/macOS; installed codex-cli 0.159.2; docker CLI present, but /var/run/docker.sock does not exist and no Linux Docker daemon is available.
validation.tests: tests/test_docker_seccomp.py: offline pinned-baseline/delta and argument checks; Linux libseccomp plus compiled kernel errno/compat-ABI probes if available; opt-in actual Docker/Codex test fails rather than skips on confinement failure after opting in.
validation.authoring_result: uv run --no-sync pytest -q -rs tests/test_docker_seccomp.py: 35 passed, 4 skipped. Two native Linux/libseccomp tests and two opt-in Docker tests were not run. Embedded Docker-smoke Python parsed successfully; its Linux execution remains unverified.
